key_insight: CODEC uses sparse autoencoders to decompose a network's computation into a small number of sparse, human-interpretable contribution components, enabling direct (causal) attribution of how hidden neurons drive outputs.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between correlational concept-discovery and causal attribution by providing a compact, causally meaningful decomposition of how hidden activations produce network outputs.
method: Train sparse autoencoders to represent hidden-layer activations as sparse contribution codes that map to output changes.
Factor network computations into a small set of sparse contribution modes so each mode corresponds to a localized, interpretable effect on outputs.
Use the decomposition to perform causal-style analyses (e.g., targeted interventions or counterfactuals) to verify how specific modes or neurons drive output behavior.
impact: Gives practitioners a practical tool to diagnose, debug, and control neural models by turning distributed activations into a few causally meaningful components, improving interpretability, robustness analysis, and targeted model editing.
visual_elements: Schematic network diagram showing hidden neurons decomposed into a few colored contribution modes that flow to outputs
Before/after intervention panels illustrating how disabling a specific contribution mode changes the output (causal test)
Bar or waterfall chart of sparse contribution magnitudes for a single prediction (ranking neuron/mode importance)
Matrix visualization linking contribution modes to input features and outputs (sparse coding heatmap)
paper_title: Causal Interpretation of Neural Network Computations with Contribution Decomposition
paper_authors: Joshua Brendan Melander, Zaki Alaoui, Shenghua Liu, Surya Ganguli, Stephen A. Baccus
